items.explanation: Reagan promised to shrink government, but his program paired steep tax cuts with a massive peacetime military buildup. Revenues fell while defense spending soared, and the deficit ballooned, tripling the national debt across his presidency. Critics argued the results contradicted the small-government promise. Option A is wrong because welfare programs were trimmed, not eliminated. Option C is wrong because Reagan deregulated rather than expanding regulation. Option D is wrong because his New Federalism did shift some programs and revenue to the states.

option_explanations.A: Wrong: welfare was trimmed, not eliminated.
option_explanations.B: Correct: tax cuts plus the defense buildup sharply increased the deficit.
option_explanations.C: Wrong: Reagan reduced regulation rather than increasing it.
option_explanations.D: Wrong: New Federalism did transfer some authority to states.

options: (A) The complete elimination of federal welfare programs.
(B) A sharp rise in the federal deficit as tax cuts combined with a major defense buildup.
(C) A sustained increase in federal regulation of business across airlines, banking, and energy.
(D) The transfer of no new authority to the states.
items.stem: Which of the following developments most undercut Reagan's promise to shrink the federal government's footprint?

items.explanation: The table shows Democrats holding comfortable House majorities through 1992, then losing them in the 1994 midterms, the first Republican House majority in forty years, built on the Contract with America campaign. Republicans then held narrow majorities through 2000. Option A is wrong because Democrats controlled the House for most of the period shown. Option B is wrong because Democratic seat totals fell over time. Option D is wrong because Republicans held the majority continuously after 1994, not in alternation.

option_explanations.A: Wrong: Democrats held the House from 1980 through 1992.
option_explanations.B: Wrong: Democratic seat totals declined across the period.
option_explanations.C: Correct: the 1994 election flipped the House to Republicans, who kept it through 2000.
option_explanations.D: Wrong: Republicans held the majority in every Congress after 1994.

options: (A) Republicans controlled the House throughout the entire period.
(B) Democrats gained House seats in every election shown.
(C) Democrats held the House until 1994, when Republicans won a majority and kept it through 2000.
(D) The two parties split control of the House evenly after 1994, alternating the speakership with each new Congress.
items.stem: Which of the following conclusions is best supported by the table?
items.stimulus: Seats held in the U.S. House of Representatives (approximate figures): 1980, Democrats 243, Republicans 192; 1984, Democrats 253, Republicans 182; 1988, Democrats 260, Republicans 175; 1992, Democrats 258, Republicans 176; 1994, Republicans 230, Democrats 204; 2000, Republicans 221, Democrats 212.

items.explanation: Winning Congress gave Republicans under Newt Gingrich the power to drive the Contract with America: balanced-budget pressure, tax cuts, and welfare reform. President Clinton, needing to deal with the new majority, signed the 1996 welfare reform law replacing open-ended federal aid with time-limited, work-conditioned assistance. Option B is wrong because Democrat Bill Clinton still held the presidency, so government remained divided. Option C is wrong because deficits shrank only later in the decade amid a booming economy. Option D is wrong because Clinton's health-care plan died in Congress in 1994.

option_explanations.A: Correct: the new majority pushed the Contract agenda, including 1996 welfare reform and a proposed (never ratified) balanced-budget amendment.
option_explanations.B: Wrong: Clinton's presidency kept government divided.
option_explanations.C: Wrong: deficit reduction came later and from economic growth as well as policy.
option_explanations.D: Wrong: the Clinton health plan failed in 1994.

options: (A) The Contract with America agenda, including the 1996 welfare reform law and a proposed balanced-budget amendment.
(B) Unified one-party control of the federal government under Republican leadership, with the GOP holding the presidency and both houses of Congress.
(C) The immediate elimination of the federal deficit.
(D) Passage of the Clinton health-care plan.
items.stem: The 1994 Republican takeover of Congress most directly enabled which of the following?

items.explanation: The congressional Republicans of the 1990s, heirs to Reagan, championed welfare reform, lower marginal tax rates, and abortion restrictions, and they backed free-trade agreements like NAFTA. Raising tariffs to shield industries clashed with that free-trade commitment, which held that open markets helped American consumers and exporters. Option A is true: they passed the 1996 welfare reform. Option B is true: cutting income taxes was central to their agenda. Option C is true: restricting abortion drew their evangelical supporters.

option_explanations.A: True: congressional Republicans passed welfare reform in 1996.
option_explanations.B: True: tax cuts were central to their program.
option_explanations.C: True: abortion restrictions were a core social-conservative goal.
option_explanations.D: Correct as the exception: they favored free trade over protective tariffs.

options: (A) Reforming federal welfare programs by replacing open-ended aid with time limits and work rules.
(B) Cutting marginal income tax rates.
(C) Restricting abortion rights.
(D) Raising tariffs to protect American industries.

items.explanation: The September 11 attacks produced a rare moment of national unity: Congress passed the Authorization for Use of Military Force nearly unanimously, created the Department of Homeland Security, and funded the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq with broad bipartisan majorities. On security, the parties stood together. Option A is wrong because climate policy remained deeply divisive, as the Kyoto Protocol fight showed. Option C is wrong because immigration stayed one of the most polarized issues. Option D is wrong because the parties remained split over affirmative action and diversity programs.

option_explanations.A: Wrong: climate policy stayed deeply partisan.
option_explanations.B: Correct: counterterrorism drew broad bipartisan support after 9/11.
option_explanations.D: Wrong: the parties stayed divided on diversity programs.

options: (A) Policies to reduce carbon emissions.
(B) Strong American action against international terrorism after September 11, 2001.
(C) Liberalizing the immigration system by expanding legal pathways and guest-worker programs.
(D) Expanding federal diversity programs.
